summary.title: Levels
summary.one_liner: You learn how to load configurable Breakout brick levels from text files into a GameLevel class in modern OpenGL, and how to add a keyboard-controlled player paddle.
takeaways: Levels are stored as whitespace-separated integer matrices in text files: 0 is empty, 1 is solid, and values above 1 are destroyable bricks of different colors.
GameLevel::Load reads the file line by line with ifstream and istringstream, then init() builds GameObject bricks sized to the level dimensions.
Grayscale block textures are tinted at render time by multiplying with a color vector, so one texture supports many colors.
The Game class holds a vector of GameLevel objects and renders the active one by index.
A player paddle is a GameObject moved horizontally by A/D keys, scaled by delta time, and clamped at the screen edges.
summary.summary: This LearnOpenGL page, part of the Breakout 2D game series, explains how to design a level system. It defines a GameLevel class that loads a grid of brick codes from a text file, with 0 for empty, 1 for solid, and higher numbers for colored destroyable bricks. The code walks through the Load and init functions, then shows how the Game class stores four levels and renders the active one. It finishes by adding a player paddle controlled by keyboard input with edge clamping.
